title.narrative: Philippines Third Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan

description.narrative: The Philippines is highly vulnerable to adverse natural events that creates risk to its recent achievements in poverty reduction and can negatively affect economic growth and debt sustainability. Across its 7,641 islands, the Philippines is exposed to multiple natural hazards including typhoons, earthquakes, flooding, storm surges, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions and landslides. Close to 74 percent of the population is vulnerable to natural disasters and 60 percent of total land area is exposed to multiple hazards. Over the past decade, the World Bank (WB) has actively supported the Government's Reform Program through a series of lending operation and analytical work. The Bank engagement on Disaster Risk Management (DRM) commenced with a first Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan (DPL) with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (CAT-DDO) in 2011. This was the first of its kind for the Asia-Pacific region. The operation was accompanied by a comprehensive technical assistance (TA) program that supported the implementation of the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act. The TA contributed to the creation of DRRM offices at the local level and helped build capacity of the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) and key agencies in integrating disaster risk reduction measures, as well as tracking the use of the DRRM funds. The program also supported the Department of Finance (DOF) in developing a National Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance (DRFI) strategy. In 2015, CAT-DDO2 was approved with a dual objective to: (i) strengthen risk reduction investment planning and regulations and; (ii) enhance the financial capacity to manage disaster risk. TA supported its complex reforms focused on developing tools to enhance the socioeconomic resilience of provinces for better planning and investment programming, improving the outdated national building regulations to include disaster risk reduction and climate resilience measures, and strengthening financial preparedness to disasters. The loan was fully drawn down in 2018 following Tropical cyclone Mangkhut.

The development objective is to strengthen the policy and institutional capacity of the Government of the Philippines to reduce disaster risk, respond to and recover from natural disasters. This will be achieved by supporting policy actions aimed at further (i) strengthening the policy, regulations and institutional framework for disaster risk reduction; and (ii) enhancing the capacity to respond and recover from disasters.

title.narrative: Using GeoRiskPH, climate resilience and disaster risk reduction measures are integrated in the local DRRM plans of LGUs

comment.narrative: <p><em>Target exceeded (108%</em><em>).</em> 108 LGUs used GeoRiskPH to integrate climate resilience and disaster risk reduction (DRR) measures in their local DRRM plans. LGUs use GeoRiskPH to access updated hazard information and integrate DRR measures intotheir local DRRM plans. The platform enabled them to generate risk information and prioritize programs, projects, and activities based on science-based vulnerability and exposure risk maps. The full list of 108 LGUs is available in the project files. Information source: Office of Civil Defense.</p>

title.narrative: The use of GeoRiskPH for the prioritization of public infrastructure projects by key Government agencies

comment.narrative: <p><em>Target exceeded (300%)</em><em>.</em> The 15 agencies are: (i) Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), (ii) Department of Health (DOH), (iii) Department of Education (DepEd), (iv) Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), (v) Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB), (vi) Climate Change Service, (vii) National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA), (viii) Department of Environment and Natural Resources- Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB), (ix) Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA); (x) Office of Civil Defense (OCD); (xi) Social Housing Finance Corporation (SHFC), (xii) National Home Mortgage Finance Corporation (NHMFC), (xiii) Department of Agriculture- Bureau of Animal Industry (DA-BAI), (xiv) Office of the President- Presidential Management Staff (OP-PMS), and (xv) Advanced Science and Technology Institute (ASTI). The NGAs use the GeoRiskPH platform to prioritize resilient infrastructure investments by accessing vital hazard and risk information. For instance, the DPWH uses it to prioritize flood control projects, while DepEd uses it to identify interventions to enhance the resilience of school buildings. The platform also allowed the NGAs to upload baseline information and share exposure information with other entities and the public. Information source: Department of Science and Technology- Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (DOST-PHIVOLCS).</p>

title.narrative: Capacity of LGUs to formulate local disaster rehabilitation and recovery programs has been enhanced

comment.narrative: <p><em>Exceeded (197%</em><em>) target.</em> Staff from 197 LGUs were trained by the R2R Rehabilitation and Recovery Training Program from April 2021 to February 2022 on pre-disaster rehabilitation and recovery planning. Following the training, these LGUs developed their respective (i) Local Baseline Data for DRR and (ii) Local Disaster Rehabilitation and Recovery Plan. The full list of 197 LGUs is available in the project files. Information source: Office of Civil Defense (OCD)</p>

title.narrative: Local DRF strategies to finance post-disaster recovery have been developed

comment.narrative: <p><em>Target exceeded (197%</em><em>) target. </em>Staff from the above 197 trained LGUs were trained and developed local DRFstrategies to finance post-disaster recovery, which enabled them to identify and expand financing options for financing rehabilitation programs and projects beyond traditional sources, such as the Local DRRM Fund and the National DRRM Fund; and helped enhance their financial preparedness to speed up recovery efforts. Information source: OCD</p>

title.narrative: Implementation of the ECT Program by DSWD in disaster affected areas

comment.narrative:
<p><em>Target exceeded (600%</em><em>)</em>. An ECT Program Manual of Operations was developed in 2019 and implemented by DSWD. TheECT program was implemented upon declaration of a state of calamity and used to respond to Severe Tropical Storm Maring (October 2021), Abra Earthquake (July 2022), Typhoon Karding (September 2022), Super Typhoon Paeng (November 2022), Cordillera Autonomous Region earthquake (October 2022), and oil spill in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro (March 2023). In total, 61,455 household beneficiaries received ECT Program support. Information source: DSWD</p>
